blocking.section: Decision outcome (Logs row, Figure 1) and Decision drivers (Never on the critical path)
blocking.issue: The stdout log path is synchronous and has no bound, and the ADR never says where access logs, the busiest log stream, enter it. Figure 1 sends `log/slog handler` straight to `JSON lines on stdout`, and only the bridge output passes the bounded queue. A standard `slog` JSON handler writes to its `io.Writer` under a mutex on the caller's goroutine. `slog.NewMultiHandler`, which the Consequences cite, calls every handler in turn on that same goroutine, and the `otelslog` handler converts the record there too. So any request-path `slog` call, such as a Plugin trap warning during an error storm or anything at `RURALZ_LOG_LEVEL=debug`, contends on one process-wide lock, and it blocks outright when stdout is a full pipe (Docker's default log mode blocks). That breaks the ADR's own driver and the owning document's O2 rule. The owning document keeps access logs off the request goroutine: the request copies fields into a pooled record, a worker encodes it, and the queue is bounded to 8,192 records and 4 MiB with `queue_full` drops, within 8 allocations and 2 µs p99 (target). The ADR's single-path rule 'Code logs only through `log/slog`' with 'JSON lines on stdout always' leaves room to put access logs through the synchronous multi-handler, which cannot meet those budgets.
blocking.evidence: "| Logs | Code logs only through `log/slog` via `internal/telemetry`: JSON lines on stdout always, plus OTLP logs through `otelslog` and a bounded processor when an endpoint is set; ..."; Figure 1 edges "slog --> out" and "br --> q"; driver "**Never on the critical path (P3)**: telemetry never blocks, slows or fails a request; queues are bounded and drop with a counter". Owning document, Access logs: "The request goroutine evaluates `when` and copies every field, truncated, into a pooled record buffer for a worker to encode".
blocking.fix: Extend the Logs row: 'No request goroutine runs a writing handler. Access log records are copied into pooled records in a bounded queue (8,192 records and 4 MiB, target, per Observability), and one worker encodes each record once for stdout and hands it to the bridge. Process logs go through a non-blocking `slog` handler that enqueues into a bounded queue drained by the one goroutine that owns stdout. Both queues drop with `ruralz_telemetry_logs_dropped_total{stream, reason="queue_full"}`.' Redraw Figure 1 so that `slog` feeds a bounded log queue before both `out` and `br`. Add a Confirmation item, Planned (M1): a test that blocks the stdout pipe and asserts that request latency stays within budget while drops are counted.

blocking.section: Decision outcome (Logs and Export rows) and More information
blocking.issue: The owning document's audit export contradicts the ADR's logging rule and is missing from the decision. For OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-12, Observability chooses OpenTelemetry logs for the audit log. The Ruralz Control leader exports committed audit entries keyed by Raft index, treats an OTLP partial success as failure, retries until acknowledged and never drops. None of that can go through `log/slog`: a `slog` handler returns no export acknowledgement and cannot advance a Raft high-water mark. It cannot use the ADR's queues either, since those drop on `queue_full` or `export_error`. The audit export therefore has to call the OTLP log exporter directly, and that exporter belongs to the pre-stable Logs SDK. This is the one correctness-critical consumer of the release-candidate code the ADR otherwise keeps behind the bridge. The ADR states no rule for it, no consequence and no Confirmation, and its review checklist would flag the audit exporter as a violation.
blocking.evidence: ADR: "Code logs only through `log/slog` via `internal/telemetry`" and "spans and logs pass Ruralz queues that drop with `queue_full` or `export_error` counts"; checklist: "calling `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log` outside `internal/telemetry`, MUST amend this ADR". Owning document, Control plane observability: "The leader exports batches keyed by Raft index ... an OTLP partial success counts as failure. Export retries, so it lags and never drops, unlike TB-12 (OQ-observability-19)".
blocking.fix: Add a Decision outcome row: 'Audit export | The Ruralz Control leader calls the OTLP log exporter directly from `internal/telemetry`, bypassing `slog` and the drop queues. Batches are keyed by Raft index, retried until acknowledged, and a partial success counts as failure; this is the TB-12 exception in OQ-observability-19 | Planned (M2)'. Add a Bad consequence: the audit exporter depends on the pre-stable Logs SDK and OTLP log exporter until v1.47.0. Add a Confirmation item, Planned (M2): an at-least-once test across a leader failover with a Collector that returns partial success. Scope the logging rule to 'Code logs only through `log/slog`, except the audit exporter'.

blocking.section: Decision drivers (One correlation key) and Consequences
blocking.issue: The ADR claims exemplars but provides no mechanism for them. Choosing 'Ruralz-owned aggregates, not SDK synchronous instruments' gives up the SDK's exemplar reservoirs. The owning document's aggregates are striped atomic counters, eight per 64-byte line, and integer histogram sums added with `atomic.AddUint64`, updated with no lock. An exemplar is a trace ID, span ID, value and timestamp, 40 bytes or more, and a lock-free counter cannot hold it. Nothing in the ADR or in Observability defines exemplar storage, its concurrency, or which requests record it. The metrics memory model (300 bytes per histogram label set, hypothesis) leaves exemplars out. Exporting them over `/metrics` needs OpenMetrics exposition from an exporter that is still unselected. As written, the 'Good' consequence cannot be built.
blocking.evidence: "**One correlation key**: the trace ID links spans, logs, exemplars and the `requestId` of every problem document"; "Good, because the trace ID is the single correlation key across spans, access log records, exemplars and `requestId`."; "| Metrics | Values live in Ruralz-owned aggregates, not SDK synchronous instruments, and both the OTLP reader and the `/metrics` exporter read them ..."
blocking.fix: Either add an exemplar rule to the Metrics row, for example: 'Sampled requests only write one exemplar slot per histogram label set per collection, through a sequence lock off the unsampled path; the exemplar is exported through the SDK interface of OQ-observability-16 and OpenMetrics on `/metrics`; slot memory is added to the histogram series assumption (hypothesis)', and a Confirmation benchmark item. Or drop exemplars from the driver and the consequence, and add a proposed owning-document Open question on exemplar support.

blocking.issue: The ADR does not say whether the SDK's environment configuration is honored, and that creates a second configuration path outside the Revision. To my knowledge, the OpenTelemetry Go SDK and OTLP exporters fill every setting not passed as an option from `OTEL_*` variables. Examples are `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`, `_CERTIFICATE`, `_INSECURE`, `_TIMEOUT` and `_COMPRESSION`, `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER`, and `OTEL_BSP_*`. `sdktrace.WithResource` also merges `resource.Environment()`, so `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` adds resource attributes the Resource row does not allow. Pack section 2 limits process settings to `RURALZ_*`, and pack 8.1 says equal digests mean equal behavior except for `secretRef` values and `RURALZ_*` settings. Two Nodes on one Revision could export with different headers, TLS or resource attributes. An operator's pod environment would also quietly answer OQ-observability-2, which is blocking for TLS export at M1 and still open.
blocking.evidence: "| Export | OTLP only when `Gateway.spec.telemetry.otlp.endpoint` is set, over TLS on boundary TB-12; ..."; "| Resource | `service.name`, `service.version`, `service.instance.id` (`node.id` or replica) and, in Control mode, Cluster and Environment; never the active Revision |"; "Bad, because OTLP TLS client settings and authentication have no configuration field yet (OQ-observability-2, blocking for TLS export at M1)".
blocking.fix: Add to the Export row: '`internal/telemetry` builds every provider, processor and exporter with explicit options, and builds the resource without the environment detector. `OTEL_*` process variables are ignored; `${OTEL_...}` substitution at render time stays valid.' Alternatively, name the variables that are honored as an explicit answer to OQ-observability-2. Add a Confirmation item, Planned (M1): a golden test that starts `ruralzd` with `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` and `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER` set and asserts byte-identical resource, headers and sampling.

blocking.section: Decision outcome (paragraph after Chosen option), Consequences, More information
blocking.issue: The ADR does not settle what happens when v1.47.0 ships, and its answer conflicts with a document it depends on. The Decision outcome says logs 'move to the OpenTelemetry Logs API' after a revisit, while the Consequences say call sites never change and only the bridge wiring changes. That means `slog` plus `otelslog` stays permanently. Pack section 7 and the manifest decision say the bridge is used 'until' the Logs API is stable. The tech stack Watch list, a depends_on document, says the 'Logs SDK replaces the bridge'. An implementer cannot tell whether the bridge is temporary, which decides whether `otelslog` belongs in `internal/telemetry` for good and whether the review checklist item on `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log` will fire at v1.47.0.
blocking.evidence: "Logs move to the OpenTelemetry Logs API only after its stable release ... through a revisit of this ADR"; "Good, because call sites never change when logs move to the stable Logs API: `log/slog` is the standard library"; "so bridge wiring inside `internal/telemetry` changes at v1.47.0". Tech stack Watch list: "| OTel Logs API | Release candidate ... | v1.47.0 stable | Logs SDK replaces the bridge |". Pack section 7: "`slog` bridge (`otelslog`) for logs until the OTel Go Logs API is stable".
blocking.fix: State the end state once, for example: 'At v1.47.0 the stable Logs SDK replaces the pre-stable SDK behind the bridge. Package call sites stay on `log/slog`, and `otelslog` stays as the `slog`-to-Logs-API adapter inside `internal/telemetry`. "Until" in pack section 7 refers to the pre-stable SDK dependency.' Add to More information a proposed tech stack Watch list amendment ('Fallback: stable Logs SDK behind the bridge; `slog` call sites unchanged') and a proposed pack section 7 wording, or record the disagreement as an Open question in the owning document.

non_blocking.suggestion: 'unsampled requests create no spans' is loose with the OTel SDK: `tracer.Start` with a drop decision still allocates a non-recording span and a context value, and to my knowledge the default SDK ID generator serializes on a mutex. State that `internal/telemetry` makes the sampling decision (with the two per-Node caps) before it calls the SDK, and installs a lock-free per-connection ID generator through `sdktrace.WithIDGenerator`. That keeps the unsampled budget of 1 µs and two allocations (target) in the owning document.

Name the OTLP transport and exporter modules. The owning document's example uses 4317 (OTLP/gRPC), and the OTLP/gRPC exporters link grpc-go into `ruralzd` at M1, although its catalog row is Planned (M3) and it adds a second HTTP/2 stack (S6). Choosing OTLP/HTTP (`otlptracehttp`, `otlpmetrichttp`, `otlploghttp`) avoids that, and the research notes that v1.46.0 added `http/json` to `otlptracehttp`.

State how providers are rebuilt after Enrollment (the owning document says 'Providers rebuild once after Enrollment'): spans started on the old tracer provider must finish and flush without blocking a request.

The second APISIX citation (the 3.18.0 release blog) supports only the version. The research ties it to AI features, not telemetry. Keep only the plugin-page URL for the 'traces only' claim, or cite the research row that says so.

The body is 1,483 of 1,500 words by the manifest counting rule. The fixes above need room, so shorten the Pros and cons bullets that repeat the Consequences (the v1.47.0-rc.1 points) or the More information owning-document bullet. Do not cut rule content.
Also propose the depguard rule for any OTLP log exporter module (see L1-2), so the audit-export exception is lint-checked, not only covered by the review checklist.
